narrative.overview: A precision instrument carried into the field: a scholarly serif for the notes, mechanical marks for the apparatus, and one bright signal color flagging what matters. The system is retrofuturistic craft in the Field Notes tradition — a traditional medium paired with precise, forward-looking marks. The mint field is the terrain; Cardinal Red is the surveyor's flag planted in it. Everything is flat, ink-on-paper: depth comes from blocks of color and thin ruled lines, never from shadows or glass. The personality is handmade, wry, and precise. Wit lives in the copy and structure (the nav reads as a sentence: "Jonathan Sick / Is / Making"), not in decorative flourishes.
keyCharacteristics: Drenched mint field with a single red signal accent
Scholarly serif prose; uppercase mechanical sans for interface apparatus
Flat, ink-on-paper depth: color blocks and 1px red rules, no shadows
Warm and tactile interaction: generous targets, soft transitions, red revealed on touch
Inline SVG instrument marks (red circle separators, chevron) as navigation punctuation

rules.name: The Field-Flag Rule
rules.body: Cardinal Red marks, it never fills. Links, rules, icons, hovers — yes. Backgrounds, large panels, full headings — no. Its rarity against the mint is the brand signature.

rules.name: The Large-Type Rule
rules.body: Cardinal Red on Georgian Bay Mist measures ≈4.1:1 — below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for body text. Red text is reserved for large type (≥1.5rem), hover states arriving from ink, and non-text marks.

rules.name: The Mechanical Warmth Rule
rules.body: Serif for what Jonathan says; sans (and eventually mono) for what the machine says. Prose is always Skolar; apparatus — navigation, labels, metadata, status marks — is always the mechanical voice.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: If an element needs separation, give it a color block or a 1px red rule. box-shadow is prohibited.

dos: Do keep the site drenched in Georgian Bay Mist (#defff2) — there is no white-background mode.
Do use Cardinal Red (#ed2024) as a mark: links, 1px rules, SVG punctuation, hover flashes.
Do set all prose in Skolar PE at ≥1.2rem with a 65–75ch measure; keep apparatus in Enra Sans (or a future typewriter mono).
Do preserve and extend the wordplay — the wit is load-bearing.
Do hold WCAG AA: ink for body text, red only at large sizes or as non-text marks.
Do ship real photography for making/garden content — the projects are physical objects; show them.
donts: Don't use SaaS/startup landing-page grammar: no gradient heroes, feature grids, CTAs, or metric counters.
Don't build the dev-portfolio template: no project-card walls, skills badges, or GitHub stats.
Don't drift toward the minimalist gray blog: no Inter-on-white, no colorless "restraint".
Don't costume the craft: no kraft-paper textures, distressed type, or "hand-crafted" visual clichés.
Don't use box-shadow, glassmorphism, or gradients — flat ink-on-paper only.
Don't put body-size Cardinal Red text on mint without an AA-compliant treatment.
Don't imitate Card.astro — it is unused template boilerplate slated for removal, not a pattern.
